extracted.intended_audience: machine learning conference reviewers and ML researchers (ICML/NeurIPS/COLT)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and personal reviewing standards for evaluating machine-learning conference submissions (ICML/NeurIPS/COLT), emphasizing model/algorithm/empirical contributions and rigor. Intended to guide acceptance/rejection judgments and reviewer behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take reviewing seriously
rubrics_metrics.description: Take reviewing seriously: read the paper, consider implications, then decide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should thoroughly read the submission and think through its implications before forming a decision; avoid cursory judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No categorical reject classes
rubrics_metrics.description: No categorical reject classes — judge each paper on merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply blanket rules (e.g., 'I always reject this kind of paper'); evaluate each submission on its individual merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyzes a new model of machine learning
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal paper analyzes a new model of machine learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of three ideal elements (model, algorithm, empirical). Two-of-three may still be acceptable; having only this element (without algorithm or empirical evidence) is harder to accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides a new algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal paper provides a new algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a novel algorithm is one of the three core desirable contributions. Two-of-three (e.g., algorithm + analysis without empirical evidence) can be acceptable; an algorithm alone without new model or compelling analysis/empirics is weaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrates empirical effectiveness on plausibly real problems
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal paper demonstrates empirical effectiveness on plausibly real problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical validation should be on problems that plausibly reflect real-world relevance; experiments only on toy data are discounted. This empirical element combined with model/algorithm increases acceptability; alone may be insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be skeptical of incremental work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't overvalue small, incremental improvements. Prefer substantive conceptual advances or results that change understanding rather than marginal tweaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor proof-of-possibility over small quantitative improvements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel conceptual or existence results that show something is possible are often more valuable than papers presenting only modest empirical or numerical gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value sample-complexity improvements (even constant-factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample-complexity improvements are significant even if only constant-factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvements in sample complexity should be recognized as important contributions, even when the improvement is a constant factor rather than asymptotic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require substantial computational improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Computational improvements should be at least an order of magnitude to count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efficiency or runtime improvements need to be large (roughly an order of magnitude) to be considered meaningful; small constant-factor speedups are less compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount experiments on toy data only
rubrics_metrics.description: Things Langford discounts: experiments on toy data only — toy and real data behavior diverge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical results limited to toy datasets are not convincing because behavior on toy problems often does not generalize to real applications; require evaluation on plausibly real problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer analyses that drive new algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: New analysis for existing algorithms is less interesting than analysis that drives new algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic work should ideally lead to new algorithmic ideas; purely re-analyzing existing algorithms without yielding new methods or insights is less compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge reviewer bias but prioritize rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal interests: reviewer acknowledges existing research interests bias him, but considers this less important than the rigor criteria above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be aware of their personal biases and disclose them, but prioritize objective rigor-related standards (model/algorithm/empirics, sample complexity, substantial computational gains) when judging papers.
